newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open stronger in wake of U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open stronger in wake of U.S. data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened stronger on Tuesday and outperformed their U.S. counterparts as the release of weaker than expected U.S. retail sales data reduced expectations that U.S. rates would rise soon, analysts said.

"We bumped up when the U.S. bumped up," said Michael Gregory, a fixed-income economist and strategist with Lehman Brothers Canada Inc. "We've followed that and we've done even a little bit better. As well, the currency has firmed up a little bit here."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.10 to C$110.95 to yield 7.073 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 1/32 to yield 6.88 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to 19 basis points from 20 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.

Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets strengthened on Tuesday after the U.S. Commerce Department said retail sales fell 0.3 percent in April and fell 0.1 percent less auto sales. Sales were expected to fall 0.3 percent overall and rise 0.1 percent less auto sales.
"It sort of confirms the view that the U.S. economy is slowing down and the Fed might not have to tweak it anymore in terms of higher rates," said Gregory.

The U.S. Federal Reserve's rate-setting Open Market Committee meets May 20 to decide whether to hike U.S. rates for a second time this year. A U.S. rate hike would likely weigh on Canadian bonds and the currency.
Both Canadian and U.S. bonds pared some gains made immediately following the release of this morning's data as traders sold into the rally.

In other economic news, Canadian new motor vehicle sales rose 8.5 percent seasonally adjusted in March, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday. A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 4.7 percent rise in March.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.10 to C$103.30 to yield 6.523 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 1/32 to yield 6.66 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds widened to 14 basis points from 11 basis points at Monday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 3.03 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.22 percent.
